name: klew
description: Read-only Kubernetes investigation for Claude: a verdict on what failed and why, plus logs, event history, rollout diffs and resource lookups, precomputed and compact.
long_description:
Klew gives Claude a read-only Kubernetes investigator. Instead of pasting raw `kubectl` output into the conversation, Claude gets answers Klew has already worked out on your machine: what failed, why, what changed and what to check next.

**What Claude can do with Klew**

- **Investigate a namespace or workload.** Klew collects pods, events, container logs and rollout history, watches briefly, folds thousands of log lines into a few patterns, links events to those patterns and to field-level diffs between revisions, and returns a verdict: status, leading signal, likely trigger, causal chain, confidence, every unhealthy workload with its key facts, failing pods and next checks.
- **Dig into the evidence.** Page through an investigation's pods, scored signals, log and event patterns, evidence board, timeline and live evidence without collecting again.
- **Find what changed.** Revision history of Deployments, StatefulSets, DaemonSets and Helm releases, with field-level diffs of image, env, resources and probes.
- **Read event history.** Events for a namespace or object, including ones Kubernetes has already expired (it keeps them about an hour) when the Klew desktop app recorded them.
- **Read logs.** Recent lines of one container, including the last crashed instance, masked for common credential shapes.
- **Look things up.** List objects of any type, custom resources included, like `kubectl get`, and get one object's summary, conditions, container states and optionally its YAML.
- **Use your own checks.** Your collectors and rules (YAML with CEL) run inside every investigation, and their findings join the built-in ones. Claude can list which loaded and why any were skipped.

**Safe by design**

Every tool is read-only: Klew only lists, gets and watches, and no tool creates, changes, deletes, scales, execs or port-forwards. Access is limited by the RBAC of your kubeconfig context. Suggested commands come back as text for you to review; Klew never runs them.

**Private and light on context**

Klew runs entirely on your machine with your kubeconfig. Results are compact (patterns instead of raw logs, capped lists), so they use little of Claude's context. Secret values are never returned, and common credential shapes and email addresses are masked before results leave Klew; this is best effort and can miss sensitive values. Turn on **Leave out log samples** to keep raw container log text out of results entirely.

**Add your own checks**

Collectors tell Klew to read a type of object (for example cert-manager Certificates); rules say when one is a problem.

1. Write Collector and Rule files (YAML). Start from the examples: https://github.com/glnreddy421/klew/tree/main/extensions-examples
2. Save them in `~/Library/Application Support/Klew/extensions`, or pick any folder under **Extensions folder** in this extension's settings.
3. Turn the extension off and on, then ask Claude: "Which Klew extensions are loaded?"

**Settings**

Leave **Kubeconfig** and **Default kube context** empty to use `KUBECONFIG` or `~/.kube/config` and its current context. Cloud logins (`aws`, `gcloud`, `kubelogin`) work as they do in your terminal.

tools.name: klew_investigate
tools.description: Investigate a namespace or workload and return a verdict: status, leading signal, likely trigger, causal chain, confidence, every unhealthy workload, failing pods, log and event patterns, and next checks.

tools.name: klew_investigation_details
tools.description: Page through an investigation's pods, signals, log and event patterns, evidence board, timeline and live evidence without collecting again.

tools.name: klew_workload_changes
tools.description: What changed: revision history of a Deployment, StatefulSet, DaemonSet or Helm release with field-level diffs.

tools.name: klew_event_history
tools.description: Events for a namespace or object, newest first, including ones Kubernetes already expired when the Klew desktop app recorded them.

tools.name: klew_pod_logs
tools.description: Recent log lines of one container, or of its last crashed instance, masked for common credential shapes. Off when log samples are left out.

tools.name: klew_list_resources
tools.description: List objects of any type the cluster serves, custom resources included, like kubectl get.

tools.name: klew_get_resource
tools.description: One object's summary, labels, owners, conditions and container states, optionally its YAML. Secret values are never returned.

tools.name: klew_list_extensions
tools.description: Your own collectors and rules that loaded, which files they came from, and any that were skipped and why. Reads local files only.

tools.name: klew_list_contexts
tools.description: The kube contexts in your kubeconfig. Reads the file only.

kubeconfig.title: Kubeconfig
kubeconfig.description: Kubeconfig file to use. Leave empty for KUBECONFIG or ~/.kube/config.

context.title: Default kube context
context.description: Context to use when Claude doesn't name one. Leave empty for the kubeconfig's current context.

no_log_samples.title: Leave out log samples
no_log_samples.description: Keep raw container log text out of results. Log patterns, counts and other evidence are still returned.

extensions_dir.title: Extensions folder
extensions_dir.description: Folder of your own Collector and Rule YAML files. Leave empty for ~/Library/Application Support/Klew/extensions (and folders linked in the Klew desktop app).
